title: First 10k Launch Ops Playlet
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight operational playlet to run a launch rehearsal for the first 10,000 end-users. Not a canonical launch playbook; focused on the 72-hour post-activation window and the rehearsal cadence we will run with cross-functional leads. Use for dry-runs, tabletop exercises, and last-mile gate decisions.

Scope and assumptions:
- Product surface: hosted API + dedicated fallback (model: gptx-3.2b-quant)
- Expected average request size: 420 tokens; peak concurrency modeled ~1.2k concurrent requests at T+12h
- Primary KPIs measured in this rehearsal: latency (p50/p95), error rate, token burn per minute, cost-per-1000-tokens estimate, feature adoption (conversion funnel to queued preview), and quality regressions (prompt-set eval pass rate)
- Environment: staging->canary->gradual ramp to hosted (with Dedicated reserved capacity as fallback)

72-hour rehearsal timeline (high-level):
- T-48: preflight checklist complete, telemetry hooks validated, canary config ready
- T-24: dry-run #1 (low-volume synthetic traffic), confirm observability dashboards and alert plumbing
- T-6: leadership sync and go/no-go alignment -> gating decisions reviewed
- T+0: soft-open to 500 internal test accounts (monitor p95 over 30m windows)
- T+6: expand to 5k external beta cohort if all gates green
- T+24: stress probe (20% traffic surge for 15m) to validate autoscaling + fallback routing
- T+48: evaluate KPIs, run rollback / degrade scenarios in tabletop (simulate region outage, model OOM)
- T+72: consolidation, postmortem draft, observed vs expected KPI delta table

Acceptance gates (must be green to progress):
- p95 inference latency (hosted): < 350ms for short prompts, <700ms for long prompts (<=1024 tokens)
- end-to-end success rate: >= 99.5% (acceptable transient errors <= 0.5%)
- error budget: less than 10 incidents > 5 minutes across core endpoints in 72h window
- token-cost burn: within 15% of forecast for T+24 (forecast attached below)
- quality: prompt eval pass rate >= 95% for smoke prompt set v3.2
- observability: trace sampling visible in Console for at least 95% of sampled requests

Preflight checklist (owners and quick verification):
- Infra & SRE (Diego Morales): Dedicated pool reserved and test traffic routed to fallback; run one failover drill. Verify KV cache warmed for common prefixes. Verify autoscaler ramp policy set to "surge-friendly".
- Serving runtime (Liam O'Connor): Model variant gptx-3.2b-quant uploaded, quant config validated, kernel selection logs OK. Run local inference smoke with CPU fallback.
- Product (Priya Singh): Feature flags set (soft-open cohort), canary percentage ready. Confirm rollout policies and A/B tagging for telemetry.
- Devexp & Console (Janelle Park): Dashboards prebuilt: per-route latency, token-burn, cost breakdown, model-fallback counts, prompt-eval-rejections. Test alert thresholds.
- Security/Compliance (Security buddy): KMS keys present for Private mode — not used in hosted rehearsal but validated for Dedicated fallback. Audit log ingestion verified.

Metrics sheet (to be updated during rehearsal):
- p50_latency_ms: baseline 110, target < 180 (short prompts)
- p95_latency_ms: baseline 300, acceptance < 350
- 5xx_rate_pct: baseline 0.2, acceptance < 0.5
- tokens_per_min: forecast 45k at T+12h, threshold alert at 60k
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd: forecast 0.12, alert if > 0.16

Telemetry and alerts (quick config):
- Primary alert: sustained p95 > 400ms for 3 consecutive 5m windows -> Ops notify + auto-scale check
- Secondary alert: 5xx rate > 1% for 10m -> Pager to SRE
- Cost burn alert: projected monthly burn deviation > 30% -> Finance + Product
- Quality regression: prompt eval fail delta +5% vs baseline -> model rollback candidate

Runbook snippets (rapid actions):
- If p95 latency breach: check node-level GPU saturation -> if saturation detected, switch routing to Dedicated fallback pool (policy: prefer cheaper-compatible variant) and enable prefix caching for top 10 prefixes. Notify Product immediately.
- If error rate spike and no resource saturation: throttle ingress for non-authenticated requests at API gateway (soft cap) and escalate to runtime team to inspect recent merges (link PR checker).
- If cost spike unrelated to traffic (token-per-request jump): turn on temporary token cap per-request param and create task to analyze prompt/clients.

Rehearsal tasks and owners (table-style bullet list):
- Preflight a/b telemetry tags -> Priya (LINEAR RED-6123)
- Build stress-probe generator (patterned on real traffic) -> Serving-runtime eng (Liam) (GH PR: /runtime/pull/1987)
- Dashboard smoke and alert test -> Devexp (Janelle)
- Failover drill script -> SRE (Diego)
- Review escalation matrix and oncall slots -> Product Ops (Aisha)

Open questions / decision points:
- Do we require Dedicated for initial 10k or is hosted with autoscale + fallback sufficient? (Risk: region saturation in APAC). Proposal: start hosted w/ dedicated standby for first 48h. Need final signoff from infra by T-6.
- Token-cost guardrails: enable per-request token ceiling by default? Pros: prevents runaway cost. Cons: may degrade UX. We should test at T-24.
- Alert noise tuning: should we sample 1/10 for p95 dashboards initially to reduce noise? Ops leaning: keep full sampling for first 24h.

Post-rehearsal deliverables (owners):
- 24h/48h KPI digest (automated snapshot) -> Product Ops (Aisha)
- Incident playbook updates (concrete steps added) -> SRE (Diego)
- Quality regression report + recommended model rollbacks -> Applied ML (owner TBD)
- Postmortem draft (72h) -> runbook owner (Aisha)

Appendix: quick links and artifacts
- Smoke prompt-set v3.2 (attached in Confluence)
- Traffic generator recipe (GH: runtime/tools/traffic-gen)
- Cost forecast sheet (drive link)

Notes to self (working):
- Keep the rehearsal focused on telemetry and gates; avoid feature experiments in first 48h.
- Encourage shorter standups during T+0..T+24 (15m cadence) and a single commander for decisions.
- Save a copy of dashboard snapshots at each gate for postmortem analysis.

Last updated: 2025-11-12 by Aisha Raman (in_review)
